description: A modular, freedom-first operating system ecosystem built ground-up in Rust, inspired by Egyptian mythology. Targets mobile, laptop, and desktop with a unified codebase and two release philosophies. Currently built as a custom userspace and daemon architecture on top of the Linux kernel — see long_term_vision for the eventual custom-kernel ambition.
philosophy: Everything ground up. Every name earns its place. Every component knows its job. Nothing overlaps.

mobile.name: Osiris Ramesses
mobile.audience: General users — people tired of Google/Apple but not willing to tinker
mobile.philosophy: Stable, prosperous, just works. Sane defaults. Services managed silently.

mobile.name: Osiris Netjeru
mobile.philosophy: Exposed, divine, no guardrails. Every daemon visible and replaceable.

desktop.name: Osiris OS
desktop.note: Built first. Mobile follows after PC stack is stable.

termux_proot.name: Osiris OS (hosted)
termux_proot.type: aarch64 / arm64-v8a — Android hardware via Termux + proot-distro Debian
termux_proot.note: Primary active development target. Build and verify here before porting to bare-metal desktop or mobile hardware.

phase_1a.name: Pinephone Pro
phase_1a.reason: Best open mobile Linux target. Mainline kernel, open bootloader, hardware kill switches, community aligned with Osiris.

phase_1b.name: Framework Laptop
phase_1b.reason: Shared modularity philosophy. Excellent mainline Linux support. Target audience overlap with Netjeru users. Ra desktop battle-tested here before mobile.

phase_2.name: Sokar
phase_2.description: Ground-up hardware designed for Osiris. Modular components mirroring OPIUM package philosophy. Hardware kill switches mapped per daemon. Open bootloader by design.
phase_2.mythology: Sokar — Egyptian god of the physical vessel, craftsman of sacred objects. Later merged with Osiris into Ptah-Sokar-Osiris.
phase_2.note: Reference hardware target for the Linux-based OS. Distinct from — and a prerequisite step before — the long_term_vision custom-kernel hardware ambition.

long_term_vision.note: Aspirational, not roadmapped. Not a current or near-term stage — recorded so the ambition is tracked deliberately rather than assumed or lost.

custom_kernel.description: Sitratis' long-term goal: Osiris eventually runs its own kernel rather than Linux, with Sokar as ground-up hardware designed alongside it.
custom_kernel.reality_check: Kernel development is a distinct discipline from the userspace/daemon/orchestration work Osiris has built so far (Kha, Ma'at, Bridge, the 42 daemons, Ra). It involves its own multi-year learning curve: memory management, scheduling, driver models, architecture-specific bring-up, and boot protocol design — effectively separate from everything in this roadmap today.
custom_kernel.relationship_to_current_work: Nothing being built now is wasted if this happens later — Kha, Ma'at/Bridge, and the daemon architecture are kernel-agnostic in concept (an init process, an IPC/orchestration layer, and sensor daemons are needed regardless of which kernel sits underneath). The porting work would be substantial but the architecture would transfer.
custom_kernel.suggested_path_if_pursued: Treat as a research track running in parallel with, not blocking, the current Linux-based roadmap — e.g. starting with a minimal freestanding kernel targeting Sokar or a single reference board, long after Stage 6.

init_system.name: Kha
init_system.description: Minimal Rust binary. Mounts essential filesystems, reaps zombies, forwards signals. Single responsibility: stay alive and hand control to AkerNet Bridge.
init_system.mythology: Kha — Egyptian concept of the life-force/spirit double.
init_system.boot_chain_dependency: On real hardware, something must invoke Kha as PID 1 before it can run — see systems_layer.bootloader. In hosted/Termux/proot mode, this layer doesn't apply; Kha runs as a normal supervised process instead of true PID 1.

systems_layer.description: The layers Osiris relies on but does not itself implement — either because Linux already provides them, or because they are one-time decisions/integration work rather than novel Osiris components. Added because the roadmap previously treated these as implicit rather than tracked.

kernel.choice: Linux (mainline, kernel version TBD per target hardware)
kernel.note: Osiris does not write its own kernel at this stage. Paging, protected mode, multicore scheduling, interrupt handling (PIC/APIC), and architecture-specific bring-up are all handled by Linux. See long_term_vision.custom_kernel for the eventual aspiration to change this.

bootloader.status: NOT YET ADDRESSED — real gap, flagged 2026-07-17

candidates.arm_mobile: U-Boot — standard for Pinephone Pro and most ARM mobile targets
candidates.x86_desktop: GRUB or systemd-boot — standard for Framework/x86_64

bootloader.hosted_environment_note: Does not apply to Termux/proot — Android's boot chain already completes before Termux starts; Kha runs as a hosted process, not true PID 1, in this environment.
open_questions: Secure boot posture — supported, required, or explicitly rejected per Osiris's freedom-first philosophy?
Who invokes Kha specifically — initramfs handoff, direct kernel cmdline init= parameter, or something else?

libc.status: NOT YET ADDRESSED — real gap, flagged 2026-07-17
libc.choice_needed: glibc (default, maximum compatibility) vs musl (smaller, static-linking friendly) — decision needed, not implementation; this is a dependency choice most userspace binaries link against.
libc.harvester_relevance: Harvester's existing harvest-from-Debian-proot mechanism is the natural path to obtain this rather than building it — same as coreutils/bash below.

core_userspace_tools.status: NOT YET ADDRESSED — real gap, flagged 2026-07-17
core_userspace_tools.acquisition_path: Harvester's harvest mechanism (already implemented — recursive ldd + dpkg dependency walk from Debian proot) is designed exactly for pulling these in as .osr packages rather than writing them from scratch.

filesystem_and_partitioning.status: NOT YET ADDRESSED — real gap, flagged 2026-07-17
needed_decisions: Default filesystem (ext4 vs btrfs — mountd already has partial awareness of both)
Partition scheme for bare-metal targets (Pinephone Pro, Framework, Sokar)
Standard directory layout convention (mountd already depends on /etc/fstab existing, which assumes a layout that's never been formally specified)
filesystem_and_partitioning.block_layer_note: The block layer (how the kernel talks to physical storage before any filesystem exists on top of it) is handled by Linux — Osiris needs to make layout/format decisions, not implement block-device handling.

the_abyss_network.description: 42 daemons across 9 domains. The foundation everything runs on. Unseen, modular, everything depends on it.
the_abyss_network.mythology: The Abyss (Nun) — primordial void everything emerged from. The 42 Assessors of Ma'at — divine judges at the weighing of the soul. The OS declares itself to 42 daemons before it lives.

daemons.name: gpiod
daemons.responsibility: Hardware kill switch states, GPIO events

daemons.name: inputd
daemons.responsibility: Unified input via libinput. Keyboard, mouse, touch, stylus.

daemons.name: usbd
daemons.responsibility: USB OTG, hotplug, gadget mode switching

daemons.name: displayd
daemons.responsibility: Output management, external display routing, convergence trigger

daemons.name: voiced
daemons.responsibility: Call audio, noise cancellation, mic routing

daemons.name: updated
daemons.note: depends_on no longer includes 'opium' as of 2026-07-17 fix — OPIUM is a CLI binary, not a daemon that registers with Bridge.

akernet.name: AkerNet Bridge
akernet.description: Command/control abstraction layer. Spawned by Kha. Orchestrates all 42 daemons via dependency graph. Owns the network domain entirely.
akernet.note: Standalone 'akernet' (Kotlin Android app / broader network layer) removed from this roadmap 2026-07-17 — component going forward is akernet-bridge specifically.
akernet.mythology: Aker — Egyptian god of the earth and horizon, guardian of transitions.

ra.name: Ra

modes.desktop: Floating windows, panel, keyboard shortcuts. Default on Framework/desktop.
modes.mobile: Fullscreen app management, gesture navigation, status bar.
modes.convergence: Auto-switches on external display + peripheral detection via convergenced daemon.

ra.description: The compositor and visual shell of Osiris. One codebase across phone, laptop, and desktop.
ra.note: External ~/projects/ra (older X11/x11rb window manager) has been folded into the in-repo ra workspace as the porting source — Wayland/wlroots rewrite work happens here going forward, not as a separate external reconciliation task.
ra.mythology: Ra — Egyptian sun god. The light of Osiris.

opium.name: OPIUM
opium.description: High-level package manager. Resolves dependencies, manages repos, handles upgrades. Calls Harvester underneath.

harvester.name: Harvester
harvester.description: Low-level package handler. Installs raw .osr packages, maintains package database. No dependency resolution — that's OPIUM's job.
harvester.mobile_role: APK extractor from existing Android installs + Waydroid bridge for running extracted apps inside Osiris.
harvester.pc_role: dpkg-equivalent. Touches the filesystem directly. OPIUM calls it.
harvester.status_note: Security audit completed 2026-07-17 — critical fixes (tar-slip path traversal, non-functional remove) identified and remediated; see current_status.

package_format.name: Osiris Package
package_format.description: Native Osiris package format. Every .osr carries the Osiris name. Managed by Harvester, orchestrated by OPIUM.

anubis.name: Anubis
anubis.description: System management UI. Manages processes, storage, users, system health. Built after the core stack is stable.
anubis.mythology: Anubis — Egyptian god of the dead, guardian and judge of souls.

thoth.name: Thoth
thoth.description: Native Osiris text editor. Built inside Osiris, for Osiris.
thoth.mythology: Thoth — Egyptian god of writing, knowledge, and scribes.

heka.name: Heka
heka.mythology: Heka — Egyptian god of magic and medicine.
heka.status: Legacy IDE source moved in-repo to heka/ 2026-07-17 — reconciliation with Heka naming/product boundary happens from here going forward, not as an external-import task.
heka.note: Simple yet better than VS Code.

current_status.summary: Osiris is a Rust workspace with SystemCore fully implemented (6/6 daemons), Bridge/Ma'at security-hardened following a full audit (SO_PEERCRED auth, real restart-on-failure, registry deduplication, logd forwarding), and Kha implemented with Bridge-restart-with-backoff policy. Harvester has completed a security audit identifying two critical bugs (tar-slip path traversal, non-functional file removal) — fixes in progress as of this review. Ra and Heka source have been consolidated in-repo from external projects; both still require substantial completion work (Wayland/wlroots rewrite for Ra, naming/boundary reconciliation for Heka). A systems-layer gap (bootloader, libc, coreutils, filesystem/partitioning decisions) was identified and added as Stage 1.5 — required before any bare-metal hardware target, not blocking continued hosted development.

implementation_snapshot.kha: Implemented — mounts essentials, spawns akernet-bridge, reaps zombies via waitpid(WNOHANG), forwards SIGTERM/SIGINT, restarts Bridge with exponential backoff (1s-30s, max 5 attempts) then fatal exit. No IPC/Ma'at surface by design — signal-only. Not yet verified as true boot PID 1 on real hardware (Stage 1.5/5/6 prerequisite).
implementation_snapshot.maat: Shared library (not a running process) — DaemonMessage/BridgeMessage protocol, 42-daemon registry with dependency graph, restart-count tracking. Recently extended with RegistrationRejected and Forward variants.
implementation_snapshot.akernet_bridge: Implemented — Unix socket daemon registration with SO_PEERCRED verification, real restart-on-failure using previously-dormant restart_count field, DaemonRegistry held directly (no duplication), HTTP surface on :7474 (/, /health, /daemons), logd message forwarding.
implementation_snapshot.system_core_daemons: 6/6 implemented (logd, healthd, timed, mountd, entropyd, kha-watchd), each independently security/correctness-reviewed and corrected — blocking-I/O fixes, ZFS parsing fix, bootstrap-buffer gating fix, process-state detection, NTP fallback servers.
implementation_snapshot.harvester: CLI workhorse implemented (harvest/install/remove/list/env). Security audit 2026-07-17 identified 2 critical bugs (tar-slip path traversal in install, remove() not deleting actual files) and 2 high-severity correctness bugs (wrong dpkg dependency query, manifest.rs bypassed during harvest) — remediation in progress.
implementation_snapshot.opium: CLI package manager exists with install/remove/purge/list/search/info/update/harvest commands, delegates to Harvester. Dependency resolution (db.rs) and remote repo fetch not yet implemented per ph.md assessment — not yet independently verified.
implementation_snapshot.ra: Consolidated in-repo from external ~/projects/ra (X11/x11rb window manager) — Wayland/wlroots rewrite still pending, not yet independently reviewed this pass.
implementation_snapshot.anubis: Workspace member present; implementation status not reviewed this pass.
implementation_snapshot.thoth: Stub text editor crate present; not reviewed this pass.
implementation_snapshot.heka: Legacy IDE source consolidated in-repo; naming/product-boundary reconciliation still pending.

notes: Only pre-existing dead-code/unused-function warnings in opium and harvester (independently corroborated, not newly introduced).
Verification performed via direct source review of Bridge/Ma'at/Kha/all 6 SystemCore daemons, not solely via agent self-report.
